title: Bertini open with nonzero first-order values at finite base points
statement:
Let k be algebraically closed and X a smooth finite-type k-scheme of pure dimension
d>=2. Let S be a nonempty finite set of closed points and U=X minus S. Let f:Y->Spec k,
j:X->Y over k, and M invertible on Y with invertible tensor pullback to X. Fix a finite
family s of global sections of M and use the maps of [def-zl-prescribed-point-system-data].
Assume every coefficient combination vanishes on S, the restriction to U generates
and defines an immersion, and the simultaneous jet map onto the product over S
of the prescribed jet modules is surjective. Then affine coefficient space has a
nonempty open O whose k-points give smooth zero schemes on X and nonzero jets at
every point of S. This asserts no high-degree existence, no coefficient-basis
property, and no affineness or dimension property of the members.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: derivative open, Bertini off S, and smoothness at S

proof.text: At each closed point of the smooth pure-dimensional scheme, the cotangent fibre has dimension d >= 2. This can be checked on its integral regular connected component, using regularity and the dimension of nonempty opens. The invertible stalk has rank one, so each jet target is nonzero.

For $s\in S$ let $j_s:V_n\to(\mathfrak m_s/\mathfrak m_s^2)\otimes_k L_n(s)$ be its first-order evaluation. Its zero fibre is a linear closed subspace of $\mathbf A(V_n)$ (in bases, it is defined by the linear coordinate equations of $j_s$). Hence $W=\bigcap_{s\in S}(\mathbf A(V_n)\setminus\ker j_s)$ is open. Choose a nonzero vector in every nonzero summand of the target. Surjectivity in step 5 lifts the resulting tuple to a vector of $V_n$ lying in $W(k)$. Thus $W$ is nonempty, and its $k$-points have nonzero first-order part at every prescribed point.

source.place: Paragraph 2, nonzero first derivative at each s is a nonempty open condition

proof.text: Apply Bertini smoothness to the smooth $k$-scheme $X\setminus S$, the restriction of $L_n$, and the linear restriction map $V_n\to\Gamma(X\setminus S,L_n)$. The vector space is finite-dimensional by step 1; its image generates and its associated map is an immersion by step 2. It yields a nonempty Zariski open $O\subseteq\mathbf A(V_n)$ on which the zero schemes restricted to $X\setminus S$ are smooth. Notice that injectivity of this linear restriction map is not a hypothesis of the cited Bertini theorem.

The coordinate ring of $\mathbf A(V_n)$ is a polynomial ring over $k$, hence a domain. Its nilradical is zero and prime, so its spectrum is irreducible. Every nonempty open in an irreducible space is dense: otherwise it and the complement of its closure would be disjoint nonempty opens, whose complements would be two proper closed subsets covering the space. Thus the two nonempty opens $O$ and $W$ are dense, and $U_{\rm sm}=O\cap W$ is a nonempty open by finite intersection of dense opens.

source.place: Paragraph 2, combining the Bertini and derivative open conditions; elementary parameter-space argument with the cited general algebraic/topological tools

proof.text: Let $v\in U_{\rm sm}(k)$. It vanishes on $S$. Its zero scheme is smooth off $S$ by step 8. At $s\in S$, in a local frame write $v=f$ with $f\in\mathfrak m_s$. The map $\mathfrak m_s/\mathfrak m_s^2\to\Omega^1_{X/k}(s)$ sends $f$ to $df(s)$ and is an isomorphism: its inverse sends $da$ to $a-a(s)$ modulo $\mathfrak m_s^2$; the identity $ab-a(s)b(s)\equiv a(s)(b-b(s))+b(s)(a-a(s))$ verifies the derivation rule. Thus the nonzero first-order part provided by $v\in W(k)$ gives $df(s)\ne0$. The nonzero-relative-differential criterion makes $H_v$ smooth in a neighbourhood of $s$. These neighbourhoods and $H_v\setminus S$ cover $H_v$, proving smoothness everywhere.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_prescribedPoint_bertini
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [Smooth (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hdim : X.IsPureDimension d)
    (S : Finset X) (hS : S.Nonempty) (hclosed : ∀ x ∈ S, IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (j : X ⟶ Y)
    (hover : j ≫ f = X ↘ Spec (.of k))
    (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] [((tensorPullback j).obj M).IsInvertible]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : ∀ x : X, x ∈ U ↔ x ∉ S)
    {I : Type u} [Fintype I] (s : I → Γ(M, ⊤))
    (hvan : ∀ a : I → k, prescribedPointVanishes ((tensorPullback j).obj M) S
      (tensorSectionsUnit j M (prescribedPointCombination f M s a)))
    (hgen : ∃ ht : Epi ((((tensorPullback (U.ι ≫ j)).obj M).freeHomEquiv).symm
        (prescribedPointRestrictedFamily M j U s)),
      @IsImmersion U.toScheme _
        (@ProjectiveSpace.homOfGeneratingSections I inferInstance U.toScheme
          (Spec (.of k)) (U.ι ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k)))
          ((tensorPullback (U.ι ≫ j)).obj M)
          ((invertible_pullback_tensor (U.ι ≫ j)).1 M).2
          (prescribedPointRestrictedFamily M j U s) ht))
    (hjet : Function.Surjective (fun a : I → k ↦ fun x : S ↦
      prescribedPointJet ((tensorPullback j).obj M) x.val
        (tensorSectionsUnit j M (prescribedPointCombination f M s a)))) :
    ∃ O : (Spec (CommRingCat.of (MvPolynomial I k))).Opens,
      (O : Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of (MvPolynomial I k)))).Nonempty ∧
      ∀ a : I → k, Set.range (bertiniCoefficientPoint (k := k) a) ⊆ (O : Set _) →
        Smooth ((prescribedPointMember f j M s a).subschemeι ≫ (X ↘ Spec (.of k))) ∧
        ∀ x ∈ S, prescribedPointJet ((tensorPullback j).obj M) x
          (tensorSectionsUnit j M (prescribedPointCombination f M s a)) ≠ 0
